item.description: Zinc-ion batteries (ZIBs), owing to their intrinsic safety and cost competitiveness, are attracting significant interest as next-generation energy storage system (ESS) technologies. item.description: Rutile iridium dioxide (IrO(2)) is renowned as an effective catalyst for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER), yet how its atomic structure governs orientation-dependent activity remains unclear. Here, we investigate epitaxial rutile IrO(2) thin films with crystallographically well-defined (110), (101), and (001) orientations and show that their OER activity follows the order: (110) > (101) > (001). item.title: Inhomogeneous mixing: from microscopic dynamics to mesoscopic staircases
item.description: Inhomogeneous mixing and the consequent mesoscopic layered structure have been observed in many physical systems, including magnetically confined fusion plasmas. Especially, in plasmas, mixing can be enhanced through turbulence spreading by intermittent coherent structures (blobs/voids), or suppressed owing to the formation of transport barriers (sheared zonal flows). item.title: Lymphatic Malformation Involving Cavernous Sinus With Sellar Extension: A Case Report
item.description: Lymphatic malformations are benign vascular anomalies that most commonly occur in the head and neck region during childhood, and primary intracranial involvement is extremely rare. Lesions involving the cavernous sinus are particularly unusual, given the absence of well-established lymphatic structures in this region. The authors report the case of a 63-year-old man who presented with headache, ptosis, and diplopia. Imaging revealed a homogeneously enhancing mass involving the right cavernous...

item.title: The 2025 KSPNO Guideline for the Diagnosis and Treatment of Medulloblastoma
item.description: Medulloblastoma is the most common malignant pediatric brain tumor. While recent advances in molecular subclassification and therapies have improved clinical outcomes, standardized international treatment guidelines are currently lacking. In this context, the Korean Society for Pediatric Neuro-Oncology (KSPNO) developed the 2025 National Cancer Treatment Guideline through a multidisciplinary task force, employing rigorous PICO-based literature reviews and evidence grading (e.g., ROB 2.0, GRADE)....

item.description: Isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH)-mutant gliomas are primary malignant brain tumors that predominantly affect young adults, and are characterized by relatively favorable clinical outcomes compared with other brain malignancies. item.title: Discontinuation of continuous kidney replacement therapy: current evidence and protocolized approaches for safe and timely liberation
item.description: Continuous kidney replacement therapy (CKRT) is a cornerstone of organ support in critically ill patients with acute kidney injury. While substantial evidence exists regarding the optimal timing of CKRT initiation, clear criteria to guide its discontinuation remain lacking. In clinical practice, decisions regarding CKRT discontinuation are often based on heterogeneous and institution-specific approaches, reflecting the absence of reliable and standardized indicators of kidney recovery. item.description: The natural products provide a foundational chemical space for drug discovery, yet their clinical utility is often constrained by intrinsic liabilities. Skeletal editing, the direct manipulation of individual atoms within a cyclic moiety, has emerged as a strategy for remodeling these compounds, but whether the exchange of a single skeletal heteroatom is sufficient to redirect the pharmacological behavior of a fully elaborated natural product has not been established. item.title: Cancer nanovaccine plus doxorubicin and immune checkpoint blockade overcomes chemoresistance and delays postsurgical recurrence
item.description: Chemotherapy for solid tumors has serious limitations due to acquired chemoresistance and frequent postsurgical recurrence. In this study, we developed a chemo-immunotherapy regimen combining a chemotherapeutic agent, a dendritic cell (DC)-activating cancer nanovaccine, and immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) to overcome chemoresistance and improve long-term tumor control. item.title: Acceptance and Feasibility of PC-Based and VR-Based "Room of Errors" Simulation in Nursing Education
item.description: This study compared the acceptance and feasibility of personal computer (PC)- and virtual reality (VR)-based room of errors (ROE) simulations among nursing educators using a single-group crossover design (N=37). Sense of presence, technology acceptance intention, and program satisfaction were measured after each modality. item.description: CONCLUSIONS: These results support elafibranor as second-line treatment with UDCA for patients with PBC and ALP >1-<1.67× ULN, with ALP normalization as an achievable treatment goal.

item.description: Sleep disorders are associated with cardiovascular diseases and cognitive decline worldwide, highlighting the need for effective therapeutic strategies. Polysomnography (PSG) is the gold standard diagnostic tool for sleep disorders. item.description: Two novel strains MAHUQ-55^(T) and MAHUQ-62^(T) were isolated from the rhizosphere soils of rice and pumpkin, respectively. item.title: Endothelial and Mesenchymal Stem Cell Balance Regulates Vascularization and Osteogenic Differentiation in Co-culture Spheroids
item.description: CONCLUSION: This study underscores the importance of balancing the proportions of MSCs and ECs in regulating vascular formation and osteogenic differentiation within 3D co-culture spheroids. Optimizing the MSCs-ECs ratio shows promise for advancing the development of pre-vascularized tissue in bone tissue engineering.

item.description: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) is highly prevalent among adults, making it one of the most common psychiatric diagnoses in this population associated with negative functional impact across multiple life areas, including romantic relationships. item.description: The electrochemical glucose oxidation reaction (GLUOR) offers a sustainable route for biomass valorization, yet its reaction mechanisms and the factors governing product selectivity remain poorly understood. Herein, we present a comprehensive mechanistic investigation of GLUOR on Au and CuO catalysts. item.title: Asia-enriched survey of spatial biology and three-dimensional pathology
item.description: An Asia-enriched survey of 239 respondents found that reported implementation of spatial biology and three-dimensional pathology varied across self-rated experience groups. Respondents identified cost, analytical complexity, limited standardization, and insufficient interdisciplinary expertise as barriers, highlighting the needs for practical workflows and computational support.

item.description: Burosumab provides treatment benefits in children with X-linked hypophosphatemia (XLH). item.title: Perceptions and utilization of digital health technologies among healthcare professionals in South Korea
item.description: CONCLUSION: Korean healthcare professionals show high familiarity with, and interest in, digital health yet report only moderate levels of clinical utilization and continue to face practical and regulatory challenges.

item.title: Translating culture into design practice: a preliminary test of a dual-cultural framework for animation
item.description: INTRODUCTION: How can abstract cultural concepts be translated into animation design practice? This study addresses this question by proposing a dual-cultural framework that integrates a layered conception of culture with a content-oriented 4P taxonomy.

item.description: Hot air-dried red peppers are consumed as spices worldwide for their color, flavor, and nutritional value. However, comprehensive metabolomic studies are limited. item.description: Angelica gigas Nakai root contains bioactive pyranocoumarins, including decursin (D) and decursinol angelate (DA), but the extent to which they contribute to the anti-inflammatory activity of A. gigas root ethanol extract (AGE) remains unclear. item.description: Eleutherococcus senticosus (E. senticosus) leaves were subjected to solid-state fermentation with Rhizopus oligosporus KCCM11948P for 120 h to evaluate changes in phytochemicals and functional properties. item.description: This study developed deep learning-based mobile software to assess the freshness of packaged raw squid using images of a colorimetric pH indicator. item.title: Interoperable artificial intelligence for food safety management systems across the food supply chain: a systematic review
item.description: Artificial intelligence (AI), particularly machine learning and deep learning, has emerged as a critical tool of food safety management systems (FSMSs). In recent years, AI has been increasingly applied to food production, processing, packaging, storage, and distribution, demonstrating clear advantages over conventional reactive strategies. item.title: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease: Pathogenesis, complications and pharmacological treatment
item.description: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is increasing in prevalence worldwide. Pathogenesis of MASLD has been considerably heterogenous. Increased hepatic de novo lipogenesis, adipose tissue dysfunction, genetic predisposition, epigenetic mechanism, and other related factors have been associated with the development and progression of MASLD. item.description: Climate change has reduced highland Napa cabbage production in South Korea, increasing demand for reliable long-term storage. item.description: Kiwifruit is a climacteric fruit, and ethylene-mediated ripening accelerates quality deterioration during storage. A total of 27 volatile compounds were identified, comprising nine aldehydes, seven esters, four alcohols, five terpenes, one ketone, and one furanone. item.title: Factors affecting the reactivity and sensitivity of colorimetric probes for iron ion detection
item.description: Iron colorimetric assays can be influenced by probe selectivity, ligand competition, pH, and redox conditions, leading to misinterpretation of iron chelation and redox activity. This study systematically evaluated the sensitivity and reactivity of three representative iron-binding probes, ferrozine, TPTZ, and thiocyanate, under different experimental conditions. item.description: Antimicrobial resistance in bacteria poses a public health challenge, highlighting the urgent need for alternative antibacterial strategies. Since phages can control bacteria through mechanisms distinct from antibiotics, they can serve as an option for controlling antibiotic-resistant strains. item.title: Causal asymmetry suggests productivity underlies scientific collaboration
item.description: Scientific productivity and collaboration are closely related, yet the causal direction between these two dimensions of academic careers remains unclear. item.title: Protecting workers from Algorithmic Management: a theoretical framework for four key protection factors
item.description: Algorithmic Management (AM) is increasingly being linked to adverse occupational health outcomes. Although previous research has focused on the risks generated by AM, the protective factors that mitigate these risks remain theoretically underdeveloped. item.title: Impact of low-voltage area burden and topological obstacles on atrial fibrillation recurrence after pulmonary vein antrum isolation
item.description: CONCLUSION: Patients with extreme TO counts (TO = 1 or ≥4) showed a numerically higher, although not statistically significant, trend toward post-ablation recurrence compared with those with intermediate counts. TO quantity varied significantly with LVA burden, suggesting that atrial substrate heterogeneity may influence AF recurrence patterns.

item.title: Factors Influencing Hospital Nurses' Patient Safety Competency: A Systematic Review
item.description: CONCLUSION: By categorizing influencing factors at the individual and organizational levels, this systematic review clarified the understanding of patient safety competency. Strategies that support nurses' individual characteristics and create supportive organizational environments can strengthen patient safety competency and promote safer care.

item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Severe condylar resorption was associated with greater skeletal discrepancy and higher OSA burden. Three-dimensional TMJ assessment may complement conventional skeletal phenotyping in adult OSA.

item.title: The endophyte Moesziomyces antarcticus RS1 improves drought stress tolerance and yield traits in rice
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: These findings establish M. antarcticus RS1 as a core seed endophyte that improves rice drought tolerance and productivity, positioning it as a novel bioinoculant for sustainable agriculture, particularly in water-limited environments.

item.title: Panel-based next-generation sequencing with copy number variant detection pipeline could increase the detection rate of hereditary colorectal cancer syndrome compared with Sanger sequencing
item.description: CONCLUSION: Panel-based NGS with CNV analysis was associated with a higher detection rate of clinically relevant variants than phenotype-driven Sanger sequencing in this single-institution cohort. These findings support the clinical utility of comprehensive germline testing for patients suspected of having hereditary colorectal cancer syndromes, particularly when CNV detection or simultaneous multi-gene analysis is required.

item.title: Dose-dependent spatiotemporal comparison of cell-assisted lipotransfer between stromal vascular fraction and adipose-derived stromal cells
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: SVF cells and ASCs show distinct temporal roles in CAL. Tailored dosing and cell-type selection may optimize clinical fat grafting outcomes.

item.title: End-of-life care patterns associated with hospital-based palliative care consultation: a single-center cohort with national data linkage
item.description: CONCLUSION: Hospital-based palliative care consultation was associated with higher rates of advance care planning and hospice use, lower use of high-intensity EOL interventions, and modestly lower medical costs. These findings suggest that consultation-based palliative care within routine oncology workflows may meaningfully influence EOL care delivery.

item.title: Early clinical outcomes of the trans-ocular threading technique for four-point flanged scleral fixation of intraocular lenses: a case series
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The trans-ocular threading technique for four-point flanged scleral fixation demonstrated favorable early clinical outcomes with minimal complications. This approach may reduce intraocular manipulation and maintain anterior chamber stability without the need for an infusion system.

item.title: The association of decreased thoracic muscle mass with unfavourable outcomes in lung transplant patients with COVID-19: a retrospective cohort study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Sarcopenia is associated with poor COVID-19 outcomes in patients within three years after lung transplantation. Assessment and intervention for sarcopenia are required to improve the prognosis of patients undergoing lung transplantation for COVID-19.

item.title: Final Analysis of the BRUIN Phase 1/2 Study Assessing the Safety and Efficacy of Pirtobrutinib Monotherapy in Patients With MCL
item.description: Pirtobrutinib, a highly selective, non-covalent Bruton tyrosine kinase inhibitor (BTKi) previously demonstrated durable efficacy and tolerable safety following covalent (c) BTKi therapy in heavily pretreated relapsed/refractory (R/R) mantle cell lymphoma (MCL). Here, we report final results from the global Phase 1/2 BRUIN trial evaluating pirtobrutinib in patients with R/R MCL, with and without prior cBTKi exposure. Endpoints included overall response rate (ORR), duration of response (DOR),...

item.title: Modulation of pentraxin 3 by vinpocetine ameliorates lung Inflammation in murine model of allergic asthma exacerbated by lipopolysaccharide
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrated that PTX3 plays a crucial role in an MGA model and that VINP mitigates MGA by downregulating PTX3 expression. Our results suggest that therapeutic strategies modulating PTX3 may be important for the treatment of MGA, and that VINP can be considered as a therapeutic candidate.

item.title: Vinpocetine ameliorates bone erosion and joint inflammation in rheumatoid arthritis via suppression of NLRP3 inflammasome
item.description: CONCLUSION: This study demonstrates that VIN mitigates structural damage in vivo and reduces joint inflammation by suppressing NLRP3 inflammasome activation in both in vivo and in vitro models, supporting its potential as a therapeutic candidate for rheumatoid arthritis.

item.title: Measuring Perceived Stress in Healthy Adults in Daily Life: Scoping Review of Smartphone-Based Self-Assessment
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Smartphone-based stress assessment is widespread but methodologically heterogeneous. This review provides an updated methodological overview to support researchers in selecting or developing robust smartphone-based measures of perceived stress. Only a small minority of studies reported formal psychometric evaluations, highlighting the need for more systematic validation of smartphone-based stress assessment.

item.title: A Threefold Symmetric NDI-Nanohoop With a Large Stokes Shift: A Red-Emitting Dye for Inorganic Electroluminescence
item.description: Nanohoops with radial π-conjugation, such as cycloparaphenylenes (CPPs), exhibit intrinsically large Stokes shifts arising from excited-state symmetry breaking. However, their integration into functional electroluminescent platforms has remained largely unexplored. Herein, we report the synthesis of a threefold symmetric naphthalenediimide (NDI)-embedded CPP analogue ([3]CDPNDI) and its application in inorganic powder electroluminescence (iEL) devices. [3]CDPNDI was obtained in only four steps...

item.title: Tyrosine kinase inhibitors are associated with reduced AML transformation in systemic mastocytosis with myeloid neoplasm
item.description: In an international registry analysis of 201 patients with SM-AHN, KIT D816V-selective TKI exposure was associated with longer overall survival (37.9 vs 17.8 months; P <.001) and lower 36-month incidence of acute myeloid leukemia transformation (5.9% vs 27.1%; P <.001).

item.title: Domain Swapping Reveals Direction-Dependent Compatibility of Fungal Polyketide Synthase-Nonribosomal Peptide Synthetase Off-Loading Domains
item.description: Two fungal natural products, hirsutellone and didymellamide, are proposed to be biosynthesized from closely related β-ketoamide intermediates despite producing structurally distinct cyclic products. This unusual biosynthetic relationship raises the question of whether the corresponding polyketide synthase-nonribosomal peptide synthetase (PKS-NRPS) off-loading domains are functionally interchangeable. Here, we identified and characterized HirA, a PKS-NRPS involved in hirsutellone biosynthesis,...

item.title: Impact of treated wastewater irrigation on soil pollution-induced community tolerance and microbiome dynamics
item.description: The reuse of treated wastewater (TWW) for agriculture is widespread in arid regions, but its comparative short- and long-term impacts on soil and microbiome remain poorly understood. This study aims to evaluate the short-term (4-5 years) and long-term (20-25 years) effects of TWW irrigation on soil physico-chemical properties, bacterial community structure, and emergence of contaminant tolerance in Cebala Borj Touil (Tunisia). Samples from irrigated and non-irrigated control soils (n = 4) were...

item.title: Initial experience of robot-assisted lung resection using the hinotori™ surgical robot system
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Robot-assisted anatomical lung resection using the hinotori™ was feasible in selected patients. Further studies are warranted to establish its comparative safety.

item.title: De novo epilepsy after the occipital transtentorial approach: association with occipital lobe injury and persistent FLAIR lesions
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Occipital cortical contusion and persistent postoperative occipital FLAIR lesions ≥ 2 mL were strongly associated with de novo epilepsy following OTA. Venous compromise, including compression of basal occipital veins and sacrifice of bridging veins, was associated with occipital lobe injury. These findings suggest that meticulous preservation of venous structures and avoidance of occipital lobe injury are important surgical principles for reducing postoperative epilepsy after OTA.

item.title: Annualized fibrosis dynamics in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease: a paired-biopsy cohort
item.description: CONCLUSION: In this real-world pre-incretin paired-biopsy cohort, fibrosis change under routine care was bidirectional and heterogeneous, with wide variation in annualized rate. These data provide a reference for evaluating how emerging metabolic therapies modify the longitudinal course of MASLD.

item.title: Reply to "Does statistical significance demonstrate a change in prognostic utility after TAVI?"
item.description: No abstract

item.description: Synthetic dye contamination negatively affects ecological creatures and health because of the durability and toxicity of dye molecules. This study aimed to isolate dye-degrading bacteria from three amphipod species, comprising Floresorchestia amphawaensis (FA), Quadrivisio meufong (QM), and Grandidierella sp. item.title: Northward shift in cancer mortality inequality across Japanese prefectures, 1995-2023, a nationwide ecological study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Geographic inequality in cancer mortality persisted in Japan, but its pattern changed substantially. The findings suggest that national cancer control should monitor subnational inequality directly and support regionally targeted strategies.

item.title: Localized Plasmon-Induced Bond Dissociation in a Two-Dimensional Metal-Organic Framework
item.description: Surface-supported two-dimensional metal-organic frameworks (2D-MOFs) are promising molecule-based platforms with tunable electronic, optical, magnetic, and quantum functionalities. However, directly correlating local photochemical responses with structural evolution remains challenging because conventional optical spectroscopies lack sufficient spatial resolution. item.title: Reversible Multi-Degree-of-Freedom Photocontrol over Chiroptical Responses of Chiral Plasmonic and Mie-Resonant Nanostructures
item.description: Chiral nanostructures have attracted considerable interest for applications in enantioselective sensing and catalysis, circularly polarized light (CPL) detection, filtering, and emission, as well as metamaterials. Dynamic and reversible control of their chiroptical properties would greatly expand their functionalities. item.title: Epoxides as the Gateway to High-Level Nitrogen Incorporation in Graphene Oxide
item.description: Nitrogen-doped graphene holds immense promise for electrocatalysis, where surpassing the traditional 2-5 at% nitrogenation ceiling requires strategic control of thermodynamic and kinetic factors. Here, we systematically investigate the dominant thermodynamic and kinetic parameters to reach higher nitrogenation. It is demonstrated that, within the investigated 140-200 °C hydrothermal regime, neither kinetic nor mass-transport limitations matter, in sharp contrast to the prevailing literature....

item.title: RPS17 can act as a tumor suppressive ribosomal protein in human cell lines
item.description: Certain ribosomal proteins (RPs) function as tumor suppressors. For example, RPL5 and RPL11 suppress oncogenesis by binding to MDM2 and thereby up-regulating p53, a mechanism referred to as the RP-MDM2-p53 cascade. However, whether other cancer-associated ribosomal proteins actually function as tumor suppressors has remained largely unclear. Previously, we showed that siRNA-mediated silencing of RPS17, in combination with expression of HPV16 E7 and activated KRAS G12V, transformed normal human...

item.title: Strengthening Japan's drug discovery and medical research ecosystem: AMED's innovation challenge
item.description: Japan continues to face challenges in translating life science and medical research into innovative medicines and healthcare technologies. The Japan Agency for Medical Research and Development (AMED), established in 2015, plays a central role in bridging basic research and practical application. To address gaps between research and development stages and to promote practical application of promising technological seeds from academia, AMED adopted five strategic priorities under its Third Mid- to...

item.title: Fermentation-derived microbial metabolite DHNA modulates intestinal innate immune responses through AhR-associated pathways
item.description: 1,4-Dihydroxy-2-naphthoic acid (DHNA), a microbial metabolite produced during fermentation by Propionibacterium freudenreichii, is known as a bifidogenic growth stimulator used in functional foods. Although DHNA has been reported to exert anti-inflammatory effects, its role in intestinal immune regulation remains incompletely understood. In this study, we investigated whether DHNA modulates innate immune responses in intestinal epithelial and immune cell models in association with aryl...

item.title: The attachment rate of Vibrio anguillarum to microplastics strongly varies with strain identity, particle characteristics, and environmental conditions
item.description: Microplastics (MPs), resulting from plastic objects and waste degradation, are increasingly abundant, particularly in marine environments. They exhibit a hydrophobic surface on which biofilms form easily. Metagenomic analyses of these biofilms have revealed that they often contain bacterial species potentially pathogenic to humans or animals. For this reason, MPs are suspected to present a risk to public health by acting as a vector for pathogenic bacterial species. To better understand this...

item.title: Bragg-Peak Luminescence of Liquid Water under High-LET Carbon-Ion Irradiation: Constraints from Nitrate and Dissolved-Gas Perturbations
item.description: The origin of the faint luminescence emitted by liquid water below the Cherenkov threshold─whether it is mediated by chemically evolving radiolytic intermediates or originates from a prompt physical excitation of the medium─has remained unresolved since its first observation by Belcher in 1953. We examine the Bragg-peak luminescence of pure water under 290 MeV u-1 12C-ion irradiation using two independent perturbations: NaNO3 addition (0-1000 mM) and replacement of dissolved air with N2. item.title: Post-Translationally Generated Cysteine-Sulfonate Functions as a Ligand in the Oxygen-Evolving Complex of Photosystem II
item.description: Photosynthetic oxygen evolution is catalyzed by the Mn4CaO5 cluster in the oxygen-evolving complex (OEC) of photosystem II. The Mn4CaO5 cluster is coordinated by six carboxylate ligands and one imidazole ligand derived from amino acid residues. However, the precise roles of these amino acid ligands remain unclear. item.description: No abstract

item.title: TurboID proximity labeling combined with structure prediction identifies C3H61/AtTZF5 as a tail-binding protein of Arabidopsis class VIII myosin ATM1
item.description: Higher plants possess two classes of myosin molecular motors, class XI and class VIII, both unique to the plant lineage. The diverse cellular functions of class XI myosins, including organelle transport and nuclear positioning, have been elucidated largely through systematic identification of cargo adaptor proteins that bind to their globular tail domains (GTDs). item.title: Ganglion cyst of the posterior cruciate ligament associated with osteochondritis dissecans of the medial femoral condyle: A case report
item.description: Ganglion cysts arising from the posterior cruciate ligament (PCL) of the knee are rare, and their aetiology remains unknown. In this case, we found a ganglion cyst of the PCL concomitant with osteochondritis dissecans (OCD) of the medial femoral condyle (MFC). item.title: Camptodactyly and Early-Onset Scoliosis in Snijders Blok-Campeau Syndrome
item.description: Snijders Blok-Campeau syndrome is caused by a heterozygous CHD3 pathogenic variant, and characterized by features including macrocephaly, speech delay, hypotonia, and joint laxity. In the hereby-presented case, a Japanese girl with Snijders Blok-Campeau syndrome displayed bilateral middle finger camptodactyly and early-onset scoliosis, beyond the characteristic symptoms such as intellectual disability, facial abnormalities, macrocephaly, and hypotonia due to a recurrent CHD3 pathogenic variant....

item.title: Successful Resection of Transverse Colon Cancer Invading a Reconstructed Jejunum After Pancreaticoduodenectomy: A Case Report
item.description: The treatment of locally advanced colon cancer is surgically challenging, particularly in patients with prior pancreaticoduodenectomy. Careful assessment after neoadjuvant chemotherapy may enable curative resection while preserving pancreaticobiliary reconstruction. As the postoperative prognosis for pancreaticoduodenectomy improves, similar cases can be expected to increase.

item.title: Altered renal aquaporin mRNA expression in early response to arsenic trioxide exposure
item.description: Arsenic trioxide (ATO) exhibits potent nephrotoxicity; however, the dynamic response of renal aquaporins (AQPs) to acute ATO exposure remains unclear. This study aimed to elucidate the expression patterns of AQPs during early renal response to ATO exposure. Male Sprague-Dawley rats were orally administered ATO (20 mg/kg/day) for one week. item.title: Neuromodulation Therapies for Depression: Current Status and Future Directions
item.description: Major depressive disorder is a leading cause of disability worldwide, and many patients fail to achieve sustained remission with first-line pharmacotherapy or psychotherapy. This unmet need has traditionally been framed as treatment-resistant depression (TRD), defined by an inadequate response to antidepressant treatment. item.title: Analysis of Merlin expression and Hippo pathway in feline and canine meningiomas
item.description: The most common genetic abnormality involved in human meningiomas, Neurofibromatosis type-2 (NF2) mutation, is associated with fibrous (grade 1), transitional (grade 1), and atypical (grade 2) meningiomas. The loss of Merlin, encoded by NF2, induces deregulation of Hippo pathway, resulting in nuclear translocation of YAP and TAZ (WWTR1) and promotes tumor cell proliferation. item.title: A comparative review of inflammatory bowel disease guidelines: JSGE, ECCO, AGA, and ACG
item.description: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), encompassing ulcerative colitis (UC) and Crohn's disease (CD), is managed according to clinical practice guidelines that integrate evidence appraisal with regional healthcare contexts. This narrative, comparative review examined selected guideline documents from the Japanese Society of Gastroenterology (JSGE), European Crohn's and Colitis Organisation (ECCO), American Gastroenterological Association (AGA), and American College of Gastroenterology (ACG) using the...

item.title: Authors' reply to "Comment on Prospective randomized clinical trial on comprehensive cardiac rehabilitation combined with individualized cognitive training in older adults with heart failure and mild cognitive impairment"
item.description: No abstract

item.title: Intraductal papillary neoplasm of the extrahepatic bile duct in a beagle dog
item.description: Primary neoplasms of the extrahepatic bile ducts are rare in dogs. This report describes a case in a 4-year-old male Beagle dog that exhibited elevated liver enzyme levels without any clinical signs. Grossly, a nodule was observed filling the lumen from the cystic duct to the common bile duct, causing biliary distension. Histopathologically, the neoplasm was characterized by papillary proliferation of epithelial cells with slight atypia, rare mitotic figures, and mucin production. Although these...

item.title: Intraoperative demonstration of a check-valve mechanism in a spinal extradural arachnoid cyst with nerve root incarceration
item.description: Spinal extradural arachnoid cysts (SEDACs) are rare lesions thought to arise from a dural defect associated with a check-valve mechanism, although direct intraoperative evidence is limited. We report a 17-year-old female presenting with persistent low back pain and bilateral lower extremity numbness. Magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated a cystic lesion at the Th12-L1 level displacing the dural sac, while computed tomography myelography failed to identify a communicating tract. Surgical...

item.title: Diagnostic challenge in distinguishing intestinal endometriosis-associated carcinoma from primary colorectal adenocarcinoma: a case report
item.description: Malignant transformation of intestinal endometriosis is rare and may closely mimic primary colorectal adenocarcinoma. A 43-year-old woman with a history of ovarian endometriosis presented with melena and a rectosigmoid tumor with uterine invasion and multiple lymph node metastases. Histopathological examination revealed moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma with intestinal endometriosis but no definitive transition between the endometriosis and the carcinoma, supporting an initial diagnosis...

item.title: Vacancy-Induced Ligand-Hole Character Redirects Oxygen Redox in Li-Rich Layered Oxides
item.description: Li-rich layered oxides access high capacities through the combined participation of transition-metal and oxygen redox, but oxygen oxidation is often coupled with irreversible structural rearrangement and voltage decay. Here, we show that oxygen-vacancy-preconditioning modifies the local Ni-O electronic structure and promotes oxygen-derived ligand-hole character in a Li-rich layered oxide. item.title: Protecting Groups as Catalysts: Direct Synthesis of Primary Amines from Ammonia under Carbonyl Catalysis
item.description: Primary amines are indispensable building blocks in pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, and functional materials, yet their direct, modular synthesis from ammonia remains challenging. Here we report a carbonyl catalysis strategy that enables the direct synthesis of structurally complex primary amines from ammonia by integrating the conventional multistep sequence of protection, N-H functionalization, and deprotection into a single catalytic cycle. item.title: Modifier-Driven Proton Conductivity in Hybrid Glasses above 200 °C
item.description: Compositional tuning is a cornerstone of inorganic glass science, yet analogous strategies remain underdeveloped for emerging metal-organic hybrid glasses. We introduce phosphate modification of zinc imidazolate glass as a route to hybrid glasses with tunable network connectivity and proton-conductive functionality. item.description: We report the synthesis and magnetic properties of one-dimensional lanthanidocenate coordination polymers, [Ln(η5-LSn)2K]n (Ln = Tb, Dy; LSn = [1,4-bis(tert-butyl-dimethylsilyl)-2,3-bis-phenyl-stannolediide]). item.title: Anatomical and molecular characterization of a regionally heterogeneous intramuscular tendon in the mouse masseter muscle
item.description: The mouse masseter muscle comprises distinct superficial and deep layers, but the tendinous tissue located between these layers remains poorly characterized. In this study, we investigated the anatomical, molecular, and ultrastructural characteristics of this tissue. item.description: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is a progressive cardiopulmonary disorder characterized by sustained elevation of pulmonary arterial pressure due to pulmonary vascular remodeling. The resulting increase in pulmonary vascular resistance leads to right ventricular hypertrophy and, ultimately, right heart failure. item.description: Freezing of gait (FOG) is one of the most disabling motor symptoms of Parkinson's disease, yet a fundamental question remains unresolved: why does FOG occur at any given moment? Most research has focused on studying FOG once it is already manifest. The present work aims to synthesize recent observations and propose a conceptual framework in which FOG reflects a dynamic process unfolding across multiple stages and time scales. item.description: CONCLUSIONS: These findings identify a shared CRC microbiome core reproducible across age groups and cohorts, alongside EO-CRC-specific signatures encompassing enrichment of virulence-associated genes (bft, fadA), colibactin-producing E. coli (clbP), secondary bile acid biosynthetic genes (bai operon), and choline degradation capacity, as well as distinct metabolic perturbations including kynurenine enrichment and vitamin B-related metabolite depletion. item.title: Knowledge of oral health, health literacy, and oral-health behaviors among pharmacy students in Japan
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This study suggests that pharmacy students before clinical practice may lack knowledge of home healthcare and dysphagia/rehabilitation of OC, and that their practical HL skills in clinical settings are low. These findings may provide insights for addressing challenges in the teaching methods for OC and HL among pharmacy students in the future.

item.description: Large-scale computational analysis enhances the efficiency and productivity of structure-based drug design (SBDD), driven by advances in computer systems. item.title: Flexible cognition, perceived conflict, and self-monitoring in autism spectrum condition
item.description: OBJECTIVE: Social adaptation often requires balancing interpersonal conflict with flexible responses to others' expectations and self-monitoring. However, the mechanisms linking these processes remain unclear. This preliminary study aimed to examine whether perceived interpersonal conflict during moral-empathic judgments was associated with cognitive flexibility (CF) and self-monitoring-guided behavior (SMB) in individuals with autism spectrum condition (ASC) and typical development (TD).

item.title: Influenza-associated acute respiratory deterioration fulfilling acute exacerbation criteria in hospitalized patients with interstitial lung disease: a single-center retrospective cohort study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Acute respiratory deterioration fulfilling AE criteria occurred in approximately one fifth of hospitalized patients with ILD after laboratory-confirmed influenza and was associated with high in-hospital mortality. Unadjusted analysis also suggested shorter overall survival in these patients. These findings should be considered exploratory and hypothesis-generating, and require confirmation in larger multicenter studies.

item.title: Association of dietary diversity with frailty and pre-frailty in a general Japanese population: the Hisayama Study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Dietary diversity is associated with a lower likelihood of having frailty and pre-frailty, which may be partly attributable to the intake of energy, protein, and calcium.

item.title: Self-multilayered cell sheet generated by dental pulp stem cells provides a mechanically quantifiable regenerative graft for bone tissue engineering
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This study defines DPSC self-multilayering as a distinct, density-gated, matrix-anchored process of self-organization that generates SMCS. A novel standardized puncture-force assay established SMCS as a mechanically quantifiable, surgically handleable cell sheet. By organizing BCP granules and enhancing in vivo hard tissue formation, SMCS provides a practical regenerative graft for bone tissue engineering.

item.title: Miscarriage Risk Prediction for Women With Polycystic Ovary Syndrome Who Achieve Clinical Pregnancy After Fresh Embryo Transfer: Multicenter Development, Geographic External Validation, and Prospective Temporal Validation Study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The locked XGBoost model using routine preoutcome variables may support miscarriage risk stratification and counseling for women with PCOS with clinical pregnancy after fresh IVF/ICSI. Given cross-cohort discrimination loss and calibration drift, it should serve only as a risk-ranking tool, not for diagnosis or treatment selection. Local calibration monitoring is mandatory before any real-world clinical deployment.

item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This study shows that a pain-stratified, personalized telerehabilitation app is highly usable and feasible as an add-on mobile health intervention for patients with frozen shoulder and that it provides objective home monitoring of exercise adherence that traditional handouts cannot. After revision, patients are more likely to have decreased regret, whereas surgeon regret does not improve. These findings have implications for patient counseling and expectations.

item.title: Application of Digital Health Interventions for Cognitive Management in Children With Cancer: Scoping Review
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Although digital health interventions show promise for supporting cognitive function in children with cancer, substantial gaps remain in the current evidence. This scoping review mapped the field according to intervention modalities, delivery approaches, and functional components, rather than focusing solely on the efficacy of individual technologies. Future research should prioritize the development of multidimensional, personalized, and functionally integrated digital health...

item.title: Modulating Crystallization in Quasi-2D Ruddlesden-Popper Perovskite Materials for High-Performance and Scalable Printed Perovskite Solar Cells
item.description: Quasi-2D Ruddlesden-Popper (2DRP) perovskites offer improved environmental stability in relation to their 3D counterparts. However, their multiple-quantum-well structure and insulating organic spacers inherently limit vertical charge transport, significantly reducing device performance in scalable printed films. Herein, we employ methylammonium chloride (MACl) as a crystallization-modulating additive to overcome these transport bottlenecks in ambient printed 2DRP perovskite solar cells (PSCs)....

item.title: Photothermally Tunable Nano-Fusogen Enables Spatiotemporally Controlled Membrane Resealing after Traumatic Spinal Cord Injury
item.description: Rapid restoration of membrane integrity represents a potential therapeutic approach to rescuing cells after traumatic spinal cord injury (TSCI). In contrast to endogenous repair mechanisms, which are often insufficient under severe injury conditions, synthetic membrane-resealing materials offer substantial potential but remain constrained by limited control over membrane interactions and functional activation. Here, we show that mild hyperthermia markedly enhances the membrane-resealing efficacy...

item.title: HEPATIC ENCEPHALOPATHY IN ALCOHOL-RELATED CIRRHOSIS:A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW OF CLINICAL CHARACTERISTICS, THERAPEUTIC STRATEGIES, AND PROGNOSTIC OUTCOMES
item.description: CONCLUSION: Available evidence suggests that HE in alcohol-related cirrhosis may represent a clinically relevant subgroup with potentially distinct prognostic characteristics. However, current evidence remains indirect, heterogeneous, and largely derived from mixed-etiology populations, precluding definitive conclusions regarding a specific alcohol-related HE phenotype. Dedicated prospective studies are needed.

item.title: Quantum gases below 10 picokelvin in space
item.description: Ultracold atom platforms enable low temperatures and long free evolution times, which are crucial for fundamental physics tests and atom interferometry. The lowest equivalent temperature reported in such a system is 38 pK with a free expansion time of 2 s, achieved in atom-chip-based magnetic traps in microgravity. item.title: Obesity pharmacotherapies and cognition
item.description: Pharmacotherapies for obesity and type 2 diabetes are increasingly being evaluated for their effects on cognition and brain health. Evidence from preclinical models, observational cohorts, and clinical trials has intensified interest, but findings remain mixed. A central challenge is to determine whether potential cognitive effects arise from direct actions on neural circuits, indirect consequences of improved cardiometabolic health, or both. item.title: Equivalence of pseudogap and pairing energy in a cuprate high-temperature superconductor
item.description: The pseudogap stands out in the phase diagram of the cuprate high-temperature superconductors because its origin and relationship to superconductivity remain elusive. The origin of the pseudogap has been debated, with competing hypotheses attributing it to preformed electron pairs or local order, such as charge density waves. item.title: Targeting hormone conversion through dietary fiber improves polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome
item.description: Excessive androgens serve as a primary driver for many phenotypic features of polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS). Although dietary fiber has been shown to alleviate PMOS, its effects on androgen concentrations and the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. In a clinical trial, we demonstrated that a dietary fiber combination consisting of inulin, resistant starch, and β-glucan reduces androgen concentrations in patients' plasma. item.title: When fat adapts: From physiological remodeling to disease
item.description: Adipose tissue undergoes extensive remodeling to adapt to changing physiological demands. This plasticity encompasses changes in adipocyte metabolism and number, extracellular matrix organization, vascularization, immune composition, and innervation. When coordinated, these processes preserve energy buffering, thermogenesis, endocrine function, and local tissue support. item.title: Stacked porous NiTi structure with low cost and ultrahigh fatigue life for elastocaloric cooling
item.description: Elastocaloric cooling (eC) uses shape memory alloys (SMAs) as energy-efficient, eco-friendly refrigerants. However, cost-effectively fabricating SMAs into fatigue-resistant, heat transfer-enhanced structures remains a key obstacle to commercialization of the eC technology. We introduce a "stamping and stacking" (S-S) method for producing porous, fatigue-resistant SMA structures. item.title: Prognostic Implications of High HFpEF Probability in Patients With Chronic Thromboembolic Pulmonary Hypertension
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Assessing HFpEF probability in patients with CTEPH identifies those at high risk for this comorbidity and improves the precision when integrated with existing risk models.

item.title: Formulation and biological evaluation of a bacterial nanocellulose-based nanoemulsion hydrogel loaded with Persea americana Mill. seed extract: An anti-aging assessment
item.description: Avocado (Persea americana Mill.) seed is an underutilized by-product rich in catechins and fatty acids, with potential anti-aging properties. However, the utilization of avocado seed in topical formulations is limited by its poor solubility, physicochemical instability, and minimal skin penetration.
